Commentary.Commentary: The players are out in the middle. Paul Stirling and Ross Adair are out for Ireland. Taskin Ahmed will start the attack with the new ball.
...CHASE BEGINS...

For Ireland, Mark Adair was sensational as he scalped three wickets. He was well helped by Matthew Humphreys who took a brace, while everyone else chipped in with a wicket too. Finally, a test for this youthful Bangladesh bowling unit as they would be hoping to stand up and deliver in a low-scoring game. Chase begins on the other side.

After winning the toss and electing to bat nothing went well for the hosts as they kept losing wickets regularly and never got any partnership going between the batters. It was only for Shamim Hossain to stand up and help the team with his maiden Half-century to post a total that the bowlers might well fight for. At one stage Bangladesh was staring at an all-out under 100 but a brilliant partnership between Shamim Hossain and Nasum Ahmed of 33 runs helped the side to post 124 on the scoreboard.

For the first time on this tour, Ireland is in the driving seat at the halfway mark of a game. Bangladesh has been bundled out for 124 runs and a lot of credit must go to a proactive captaincy by Paul Stirling as his bowling changes were on point. The ultra-aggressive approach from the Bangladesh batters has backfired in this third and final T20I.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires and the Irish players make their way out onto the field. Litton Das and Rony Talukdar will open the innings for Bangladesh and will want to get off to a good start. Fionn Hand has the new ball in his hand and will begin proceedings. Let's play...

Pitch Report - There is a bit of grass around but looks like a batting paradise. Batters should look to consolidate and not lose wickets early while picking the right balls to hit and have a solid defense. They will find the opportunity to score runs and pick up boundaries.

Paul Stirling the captain of Ireland informs that they have one change. Says that it is a used deck and they will sees what happens early on. Adds that runs are there to be had and they as batters need to see what has to be done.

Shakib Al Hasan the skipper of Bangladesh says they would like to bat first as in the last two games they have done the same and it has worked well so the team would like to continue that. He adds that the side has a couple of changes with the leggy Rishad Hossain getting his maiden T20I cap for the national side. He closes by saying that the crowd has been supportive of the team and he expects exactly the same today.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Ross Adair, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Gareth Delany, Mark Adair, Fionn Hand, Matthew Humphreys (Replaces Graham Hume), Benjamin White.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Rony Talukdar, Litton Das (WK), Najmul Hossain Shanto, Shakib Al Hasan (C), Towhid Hridoy, Shamim Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Nasum Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, Rishad Hossain (Replaces Mustafizur Rahman), Shoriful Islam (Replaces Mehidy Hasan).
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favor of Bangladesh. They have elected to BAT first.

Ireland, on the contrary, have had a torrid outing on this tour so far and will want to get a consolation win ahead of the one-off Test match. They have been dominated by the hosts and have been nowhere near challenging them in either of the games they have played so far. The bowlers have failed to put an impression of any significance and the batters have let the side down as well. They need to click collectively if they want to put up any fight against this solid-looking Bangladesh squad in this fixture. Will we see an upset? Or will Bangladesh continue to dominate? We will find out shortly. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

The Bangla Tigers would be looking to seal their second consecutive 3-0 series win after white-washing the champions England before this series. Opener Litton Das has been nothing but a sensation for them as he leads the run-scoring charts after the first couple of games. The bowlers of Bangladesh have given no chance whatsoever to the Irish batters and have continued to trouble them. In the third T20I Bangladesh would be counting on their bowlers yet again as they have been tremendous under their bowling coach, the ‘White Lightening’ Allan Donald.

Hello, and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen to our coverage of the third and final T20I of the three-match T20I series from the Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium in Chattogram as Bangladesh will be eyeing a series whitewash against Ireland. The hosts have dominated the Irish in this series preventing the visitors from getting any foothold in this tour so far and already have an unassailable 2-0 lead going into the final fixture.
... MATCH DAY ...

Bangladesh have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the T20I series against Ireland after comprehensively beating them in the second match. The Tigers have looked unbeatable at home recently and are favourites to take the series 3-0. Ireland have been found wanting in all departments and will need a herculean effort just to compete in the last T20I. It was expected that Bangladesh would dominate in the T20I series against Ireland after beating them comfortably in the ODI series. However, the way they crushed the Irish in the two matches of the series so far has been incredible to see. Their batting has been extraordinary in this series, as they posted more than 200 runs in both matches and in the previous game, Litton Das smashed 83 off just 41 balls, also becoming the quickest Bangladeshi batter to reach fifty. Rony Talukdar has also been in terrific form, while Shakib Al Hasan does what he does best with both bat and ball leading them from the front. Taskin Ahmed already has seven wickets in this series, and he will look to add to that tally. They look like a strong unit and do not look like they are losing a game in their den. Ireland, on the other hand, has been below par in all the departments throughout this tour. The main problem with Ireland is their batting. None of the batters has clicked, with Curtis Campher being the leading scorer with 51 runs in two matches. Unfortunately, the others, like skipper Paul Stirling, Ross Adair, Lorcan Tucker, and Gareth Delany, haven’t done anything of note. Ireland’s bowling has looked hapless in these conditions, and things don’t look promising for them. Leg-spinner Benjamin White, who took 2-28 off his four overs in the previous game, is the one bright star in their bowling this series. They will hope that their senior players step up and at least give a good fight in this game. Will they be able to get a consolation win? Or will the Tigers register a clean sweep? We will find out soon.
